Hannah S: Hey team  my outpatient surgery claim was denied because the carrier says my spouse's plan should be primary. But my employer coverage should be primary per birthday rule (my DOB is earlier). Claim ID CLM-90122, member ID H776655443. Surgery was last week and provider sent me an EOB showing $1,200 denied as "secondary payer". Can benefits help with coordination of benefits (COB)?

Eli (People Ops): Sorry about that, Hannah. Yes we can help. Quick Qs: are you married and is your spouse currently enrolled in their employer plan? Do you have your spouse's insurer name and member ID, and a copy of the denial EOB?

Hannah S: Yes married. Spouse employer = NorthStar Tech, spouse member ID: N-55443322. I uploaded the EOB to this thread. The carrier note says "payer denied - other primary" and lists NorthStar plan.

Maya - Benefits: Standard COB flow: the carrier needs a Coordination of Benefits form and proof of spouse coverage to determine primary payer. Please send us: the EOB (denial), a copy/photo of your spouse's insurance card, date of birth for both members, and a signed COB authorization (we can provide). We'll submit to the carrier and request reprocessing.

BenefitsBot: ✅ Ticket created: #BEN-5401 "COB: claim denied as secondary, spouse plan listed as primary". Assigned to Maya. Expected initial carrier response: 3-5 business days after COB submission. Please attach documents to BEN-5401 or email benefits@redwood.com with subject EXACT: "COB - Hannah S - URGENT".

Hannah S: Thanks — I emailed benefits@redwood.com with subject EXACT as above and attached the EOB plus a photo of my spouse's card. Anything else I should ask the provider to send?

Maya - Benefits: Good. Also ask the provider billing team to re-submit claim with COB indicators and include spouse insurer info on the claim form (box 11C / claim remark depending on form). If the provider resubmits as primary to NorthStar and NorthStar pays, then our carrier will process as secondary and coordinate payment. If they won't resubmit, we can submit COB paperwork to the carrier and ask for reprocessing using the EOB as proof.

Hannah S: Provider says they sent to our carrier first. Should they send to spouse insurer first?

Eli (People Ops): Under COB rules, the provider/biller should submit to the primary payer first. Since you believe Redwood plan is primary (birthday rule), ask the provider to resubmit to Redwood with spouse information noted as secondary coverage. If carrier still claims spouse is primary due to coverage dates, we'll need the spouse's HR verification.

Hannah S: Oh right  birthday rule might apply, but my spouse's plan effective date is earlier than mine this year. That could flip priority. How do we resolve that?

Maya - Benefits: If both plans are active, primary is typically determined by plan-specific rules (birthday, active employment, which plan lists dependents). We'll gather documentation: enrollment effective dates from both employers and a spouse HR verification letter if needed. If NorthStar insists they're primary, we'll request an explanation and ask for a benefit determination. We can also use our COB form to assert member status while carrier adjudicates.

Hannah S: Ok I messaged Kevin in spouse HR to confirm effective date and to send an enrollment verification letter. Kevin, can you confirm spouse start date and plan effective date?

Kevin - Spouse HR: Hi all  confirmed: spouse coverage effective 2026-02-01. Hannah's Redwood effective date is 2026-03-01 per open enrollment. Attached is our verification letter and a copy of the spouse card. Let me know if you need formal COB form filled out.

Maya - Benefits: Thanks Kevin, that helps. Maya here  we'll attach the NorthStar verification to BEN-5401 and submit the COB form to the carrier requesting re-adjudication. Timeline: carrier will review and either reverse the denial or request additional info. If reversed, provider will be re-billed and you may receive an Explanation of Benefits showing payer order. If you paid OOP and reversal occurs, we'll help with the refund/adjustment process.

BenefitsBot: BEN-5401 updated: spouse HR verification received, COB form attached, carrier outreach initiated. Expected carrier turnaround: 3-7 business days. We'll update you here when we get a determination.

Hannah S: Thank you all. If the carrier doesn't reverse, what's the appeals route?

Maya - Benefits: If carrier denies the COB claim after review, we'll file an internal appeal with supporting documents (enrollment verifications, COB form, EOB). Also can escalate to state insurance regulator if there's an improper coordination determination. We'll track all deadlines; don't sign any balance agreements with the provider until we finish adjudication. If they demand payment, ask them to bill as "pending insurance" and collect minimal deposit only.

Eli (People Ops): One more note: keep all receipts and any statements from the provider showing patient balance. If you end up paying, upload proof and we'll assist with claim/adjustment for reimbursement. We'll ping this thread as soon as we have carrier updates. :thumbsup:
